targets.title: Wholesome foods and wholesome morals?: Organic foods reduce prosocial behavior and harshen moral judgments.
targets.evidence_quote: We planned and executed a high-fidelity and high-powered direct replication of Eskine (Eskine, 2013).
targets.outcome_quote: Overall, our conclusion is that organic food exposure has much less impact on moral reasoning than found by Eskine, potentially down to no effect at all. It is not clear why the original research reached such a different outcome.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The overall conclusion and three negative replication attempts disagree with the original organic-food effects.

targets.title: The retrospective gambler’s fallacy: Unlikely events, constructing the past, and multiple universes.
targets.evidence_quote: To help indicate the overall quality of our replication attempt, we included as a positive control an additional experiment with a well-defined effect size. Specifically, we used the retrospective gambler’s task (Oppenheimer & Monin, 2009).
targets.outcome_quote: To allay such concerns, we used a positive control, the retrospective gambler’s fallacy (Oppenheimer & Monin, 2009). In all cases, we observed the expected pattern of results.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The positive-control experiment re-tests the specifically attributed published finding in new samples, and the authors state that its expected pattern occurred in all cases. Klein et al. supplied materials and prior evidence; the paper names Oppenheimer and Monin as the finding tested.
